issues.legal_issue: When a first appellate court finds that a plaintiff failed to establish title because material proof was not produced, it should provide an opportunity to supply the proof and remand for retrial rather than dismiss the suit outright, particularly where the defendants did not appeal the part of the trial decree favourable to the plaintiff.
material_facts: The trial court found that the plaintiffs owned the disputed land and partly decreed their suit, including relief concerning encroachments.
The plaintiff appealed against the part of the decree that refused alternate land; the defendants did not challenge the findings favourable to the plaintiff.
The High Court found that the plaintiff had not proved title because he had not examined his vendor, and dismissed the entire suit.
The Supreme Court concluded that the plaintiff should have been allowed to adduce proper additional evidence and that the suit should be retried by the trial court.
issues.conclusion: The High Court's judgment and the trial court's judgment were set aside, and the suit was remanded to the trial court for a fresh decision, with the parties permitted to amend their pleadings and adduce additional evidence.
issues.legal_principle: Under Order 41 Rule 23A of the Code of Civil Procedure, an appellate court may remand a case for retrial where retrial is required. If the appellate court considers that title has not been proved because necessary evidence was not produced, it should afford an opportunity to adduce proper evidence and remand rather than dismiss the suit outright. The court relied on no earlier cases.

predicates.first_appeal_from_civil_suit: A party brought a first appeal arising from a civil suit.
predicates.title_rejected_for_missing_proof: The appellate court rejected the plaintiff's claim of title because proof considered necessary to establish it had not been produced.
predicates.opposing_party_did_not_appeal_favourable: The opposing party did not appeal the part of the trial decree that had favoured the plaintiff.
predicates.additional_evidence_can_address_deficien: The missing proof could be supplied by allowing the parties to adduce additional evidence.
predicates.suit_should_be_remanded_for_retrial_with: The suit is returned for retrial with an opportunity to present additional evidence.

issues.definition: When a first appeal concerns a civil suit, title was rejected for missing proof, the opposing party did not appeal a favourable decree, and additional evidence can address the deficiency, the suit should be remanded for retrial with an opportunity to adduce that evidence.

issues.legal_issue: In a civil suit or proceeding involving the government or a public body, the court must first endeavour to assist the parties to settle the dispute when doing so is consistent with the nature and circumstances of the case.
material_facts: The suit was brought against the State Government and local bodies over disputed land and alleged encroachments.
The Supreme Court directed the trial court to make an initial endeavour to assist the parties in settling the dispute and, if settlement was not reached, to decide the suit on its merits.
issues.conclusion: The trial court was required first to endeavour to assist the parties to settle the dispute where settlement was possible consistently with the case, and otherwise to decide the suit on its merits.
issues.legal_principle: Order 27 Rule 5B of the Code of Civil Procedure requires the court, in a suit or proceeding involving the government or a public officer acting officially, to make every endeavour in the first instance to assist the parties to settle where that is consistent with the nature and circumstances of the case. The court relied on no earlier cases.

predicates.civil_proceeding: The dispute is being determined in a civil suit or proceeding.
predicates.government_or_public_body_is_party: The government or a public body is a party to the proceeding.
predicates.assisted_settlement_is_consistent_with_c: The nature and circumstances of the case permit an endeavour to assist the parties to settle.
predicates.court_must_first_endeavour_to_assist_set: The court makes an initial endeavour to assist the parties to settle the dispute.

issues.definition: When a civil proceeding involves the government or a public body and assisted settlement is consistent with the case, the court must first endeavour to assist settlement.
